name: Inappropriate Sinus Tachycardia

prevalence.estimate: Exact prevalence unknown; estimated ~1% of population
prevalence.range: Rare as a clinical diagnosis despite potentially being underrecognized

criteria.description: Resting sinus heart rate >100 bpm (or mean 24-hour heart rate >90 bpm on Holter) that is not attributable to an identifiable cause
P-wave morphology and axis consistent with sinus node origin on 12-lead ECG
Exclusion of secondary causes of sinus tachycardia (anemia, hyperthyroidism, dehydration, infection, pheochromocytoma, drugs, pain, anxiety)
Symptoms associated with tachycardia (palpitations, lightheadedness, exercise intolerance)
Exaggerated heart rate response to minimal physical activity or emotional stress

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Persistent resting sinus tachycardia >100 bpm with P-wave morphology from sinus node, after exclusion of all secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: IST is a diagnosis of exclusion. Must distinguish from POTS (IST has elevated resting HR, not just orthostatic HR increase). Some overlap exists and the conditions may coexist.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Persistent resting sinus tachycardia >100 bpm without identifiable cause
pathognomonic.notes: Defining feature; HR often 100-150 bpm at rest
searchTerms: fast resting heart rate over 100 bpm

occasional.symptomName: Anxiety (may be both a cause and consequence)

rare.notes: Very rare; from chronic sustained tachycardia

searchTerms: poor sleep due to fast nighttime heart rate

imaging: Echocardiogram: usually normal (excludes structural heart disease)
genetic: Possible gain-of-function mutations in HCN4 channel in rare familial cases
other: 12-lead ECG: sinus tachycardia with normal P-wave axis and morphology
24-hour Holter: mean HR >90 bpm, elevated resting HR, exaggerated response to activity
Electrophysiology study: may show enhanced sinus node automaticity
Autonomic testing: may show enhanced sympathetic tone or reduced vagal tone

distinguishingFeatures: POTS has tachycardia primarily on standing (>=30 bpm increase), not at rest
IST has persistent resting tachycardia >100 bpm regardless of posture
Anxiety may cause situational tachycardia but not persistent resting elevation
IST persists even during calm states and sleep
Hyperthyroidism has abnormal thyroid function tests
Focal atrial tachycardia has non-sinus P-wave morphology
IST has P-wave morphology identical to sinus rhythm

redFlags: Resting heart rate consistently >150 bpm (evaluate for other arrhythmias)
Associated with weight loss, tremor, or heat intolerance (thyroid evaluation)
Episodic rather than persistent (consider paroxysmal SVT)
references: Sheldon RS, et al. 2015 Heart Rhythm Society Expert Consensus Statement on the Diagnosis and Treatment of Postural Tachycardia Syndrome, Inappropriate Sinus Tachycardia, and Vasovagal Syncope. Heart Rhythm. 2015;12(6):e41-e63.
Olshansky B, et al. Inappropriate sinus tachycardia. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2013;61(8):793-801.
Ptaszynski P, et al. Inappropriate sinus tachycardia: current evidence and management. Europace. 2022;24(8):1227-1236.
